items.title: Women's health
items.summary: Classical gynaecology (Stri Roga) describes menstrual, uterine and vaginal disorders, with menstruation viewed as a natural monthly cleansing.

list: Artava: menstrual blood, considered an Upadhatu (secondary tissue) of Rasa
Rituchakra: the menstrual cycle, divided into the menstrual phase (Rajasrava Kala), proliferative phase (Ritu Kala) and the post-ovulatory phase (Ritu Vyatita Kala)
Twenty gynaecological disorders (Yonivyapad) described by Charaka and Sushruta

p: Classical texts prescribe rest and dietary restrictions during menstruation. Modern understanding does not support isolation or restrictions on normal activities; rest and comfort as needed are reasonable. Menstruation is not impure.

list: Very heavy bleeding (soaking a pad or tampon every hour for several hours), or bleeding between periods or after sex
Any bleeding after menopause
Severe pelvic pain, or pain with fever
Missed periods with a possible pregnancy
A lump in the breast

p: Classically described as Rajonivritti, a natural transition associated with increasing Vata. Hot flushes, sleep disturbance, mood changes and bone loss can be managed with lifestyle measures and, where suitable, menopausal hormone therapy; discuss bone density and cardiovascular risk with a doctor.

items.title: Pregnancy care (Garbhini Paricharya)
items.summary: Classical texts describe a month-by-month diet and conduct for pregnancy, centred on milk, ghee and nourishing food. Modern antenatal care comes first.

list: Register for antenatal care early and attend all visits and scans
Folic acid before conception and in early pregnancy; iron and calcium as advised
Do not take any herbal, Rasa or Bhasma medicine in pregnancy unless your obstetrician has approved it
Avoid alcohol, tobacco and unpasteurised products

p: Charaka, Sushruta and Vagbhata describe a different diet for each month: for example, cold milk in the first month, milk processed with sweet herbs in the second and third, and ghee and rice preparations in later months; with enemas (Anuvasana Basti) in the eighth and ninth months in classical practice. The procedures in late pregnancy are not recommended without specialist obstetric supervision.
Texts advise a calm, pleasant environment, avoiding heavy exertion, long journeys on rough roads, fasting, sleeping on the back, suppressing urges and frightening experiences.

list: Vaginal bleeding or leaking fluid
Severe headache, blurred vision or swelling of face and hands
Reduced baby movements
Severe abdominal pain, fever or fits

items.title: Postpartum care (Sutika Paricharya)
items.summary: The postpartum woman (Sutika) is considered weak and Vata-aggravated. Classical care uses rest, oil massage, warm baths and digestible, nourishing food for about six weeks.

list: Abhyanga with warm oil and warm water baths
Binding of the abdomen
Light, warm, easily digested food at first, then gradually nourishing food
Avoiding exertion, cold exposure and sexual intercourse during the Sutika period

p: Classical texts describe galactagogue foods and herbs such as Shatavari. Exclusive breastfeeding for about six months is the modern recommendation. Check any herb with your doctor while breastfeeding.

list: Heavy bleeding, large clots or feeling faint
Fever, foul-smelling discharge or a red, painful breast
Calf pain or breathlessness
Low mood, anxiety or thoughts of harming yourself or the baby

items.title: Children's health (Kaumarabhritya)
items.summary: Kaumarabhritya covers newborn care, nutrition, growth and childhood illness. Kashyapa Samhita is its main classical text.

list: Follow the national immunisation schedule; no traditional practice replaces vaccination
Exclusive breastfeeding for about six months, then complementary foods
Regular growth and development checks
Do not give adult Ayurvedic medicines, Rasa preparations or Bhasmas to children

p: A preparation containing processed gold with ghee and honey, promoted for immunity and intellect in children. Its classical basis is a passage in Kashyapa Samhita on Swarna Prashana. There is no robust clinical evidence of benefit, the gold content of products varies, and honey must not be given to infants under one year (risk of infant botulism). It is not a vaccine.

list: Any fever in a baby under 3 months
Fast or difficult breathing, blue lips
Drowsiness, floppiness or a fit
Not feeding, few wet nappies, sunken eyes
A rash that does not fade when pressed

items.title: Men's health
items.summary: Vajikarana covers sexual health, vigour and fertility. Several common men's problems can be signs of other illness and need medical assessment.

p: Vajikarana uses nourishing diet, conduct and drugs (for example Ashwagandha, Shatavari, Kapikacchu, Gokshura) after the body has been cleansed, and emphasises emotional wellbeing and a healthy relationship.

list: Erectile difficulty can be an early sign of heart disease or diabetes: check blood pressure, sugar and cholesterol
Infertility needs semen analysis and assessment of both partners
Urinary hesitancy or weak stream after 50 may be prostate enlargement; blood in urine needs urgent assessment
Many 'herbal' sexual-enhancement products sold online have been found to contain hidden prescription drugs such as sildenafil; avoid unlicensed products

items.title: Healthy ageing (Jara and Rasayana)
items.summary: Old age (Jara) is described as a Vata-predominant stage. Rasayana aims to slow decline and preserve strength, memory and immunity.

list: Regular routine, oil massage, warm and nourishing food
Rasayana drugs such as Amalaki, Haritaki, Guduchi and Chyawanprash, under supervision
Achara Rasayana: calm, ethical and engaged living
Review all medicines and supplements with a doctor or pharmacist at least yearly (risk of interactions)
Prevent falls: strength and balance exercise, good lighting, eye checks
Screen for hearing loss, memory problems, depression and osteoporosis
Kidney and liver function decline with age: doses that suit younger adults may be too high

items.title: Mental health (Manas)
items.summary: Ayurveda describes the mind (Manas) with three qualities, Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, and recognises mental disorders such as Unmada (psychosis-like states) and Apasmara (seizure disorders).

list: Sattva (clarity), Rajas (activity, passion), Tamas (inertia): disorders arise from excess Rajas and Tamas
Medhya Rasayana: herbs said to support intellect, including Mandukaparni, Yashtimadhu, Guduchi and Shankhapushpi
Sattvavajaya Chikitsa: control of the mind by knowledge, courage, memory and concentration, a classical form of psychological therapy
Achara Rasayana: ethical, compassionate conduct
Depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, psychosis and epilepsy are treatable with psychological therapies and medicines
Never stop psychiatric or antiepileptic medicines without your doctor, even when feeling better
Herbs such as Ashwagandha, Jatamansi and Brahmi can interact with sedatives and other medicines

p: If you are thinking about harming yourself or ending your life, contact local emergency services or a crisis helpline now (in India, Tele-MANAS: 14416; in the US, 988), or go to the nearest emergency department.
